sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:1
items.html:
Explains: an exact interpretation of the four phases of coarseness, along the lines of the four discernments of our sages (Pesachim 25b). Phase 1: not possible and not intending. Phase 2: possible and not intending. Phase 3: not possible and intending. Phase 4: possible and intending.

Explanation of the four phases in the will, according to the four discernments of "possible" and "intending."
And in order to give an exact and broad explanation of this, I will explain it to you along with the words of our sages (Pesachim 25b, see there), which state: It was said, pleasure that comes to a person against his will—Abaye said it is permitted, and Rava said it is forbidden. If it is possible for him to withdraw, and he intends [to draw close and benefit], all agree it is forbidden. If it is not possible for him to withdraw, and he does not intend it, all agree it is permitted. They disagree where it is possible for him to withdraw and he does not intend it. Rashi explains: "possible"—it is possible for him to withdraw. "And he intends"—he intends to draw close in order to benefit, such as the scent of a forbidden thing, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:2
items.html:
Phase 1 is: not possible and not intending.
You find in their words four phases of receiving pleasure. Phase 1 is: it is "not possible" for him to withdraw, "and he does not intend" to draw close and benefit, so that receiving pleasure from a forbidden thing in such a manner, all agree it is permitted, since it is not considered receiving and willing, at a time when he has no counsel and choice not to receive it, and also has no desire to draw close to the forbidden thing in order to benefit from it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:3
items.html:
Phase 2 is: possible and not intending.
Phase 2 is: it is "possible" for him to withdraw, "and he does not intend" to draw close and benefit. And in receiving pleasure from a forbidden thing in such a manner, Abaye and Rava disagree. Abaye holds that even though it is "possible," meaning that he has the counsel to distance himself from it and not benefit from the forbidden thing, nevertheless it is permitted for him to draw close and benefit from it, because "he does not intend," meaning, because he has no desire in his heart to draw close to the forbidden thing, therefore it is not considered receiving, even though he draws close and benefits from the forbidden thing. And Rava said, since it is possible for him not to draw close and benefit from the forbidden thing, therefore it is forbidden for him to draw close and benefit, even though he has no desire to draw close to the forbidden thing and to benefit.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:4
items.html:
Phase 3 is: not possible and intending.
Phase 3 is: "not possible and intending," meaning, "it is not possible" for him to withdraw and distance himself from the forbidden thing so as not to benefit from it, "and he intends," meaning, he has a desire to benefit from the forbidden thing. And receiving pleasure from a forbidden thing in such a manner, all agree it is forbidden, for even though it is impossible for him, and he has no counsel at all to withdraw from the forbidden thing and not benefit, nevertheless, since he has a desire in his heart to benefit and draw close, this desire is considered for him as receiving pleasure from the forbidden thing, and he sins. And some say that here too Abaye held it permitted, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:5
items.html:
Phase 4 is: possible and intending.
Phase 4 is: "possible and intending," meaning, that it is "possible" for him to withdraw and distance himself from the forbidden thing and not benefit from it, and also "he intends," for he also has a desire to draw close and benefit from the forbidden thing. And here, all agree it is forbidden, this being the receipt of pleasure from the forbidden thing in the coarsest manner, for he desires to benefit, and it is also possible for him to withdraw, yet he does not do so. Therefore, this is the magnitude of the will to receive in its final phase, which is forbidden according to all, and even according to those who say, in the name of Abaye, that it is permitted in Phase 3, they agree that here it is forbidden, see there in the Gemara.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:6
items.html: And behold, we find from the aforesaid words of our sages the exact language with which to define each and every one of the four phases of the "will to receive," in a manner that hits the mark and does not miss the intended target, for they gave us four degrees, each lower than the other, in the sin of forbidden pleasure, which depends on the "will to receive" of the sinner. And in the first three degrees, which are: not possible and not intending, and possible and not intending, and not possible and intending, the forbidden pleasure is not agreed upon by all, but only in Phase 4, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:7
items.html: And we see that our sages combined two things with one another: the matter of "possibility" to withdraw and not receive the pleasure, and the matter of "yearning" and the drawing of his heart to want that pleasure, so that from the combination of these two, four phases resulted for them. And now let us take these matters and apply them to our subject, in the upper worlds, which are the roots for all the kinds of wills that exist in reality, and the upper learns from the lower.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:8
items.html:
When the will to receive was revealed in the Malchut of Keter, it emerged from Keter and became Phase 1.
And behold, Phase 1, which is called Hochma, and also Haya, there are two discernments to distinguish in it (as above, Part 2, Item 27). Discernment 1 is its first substance, and you already know (see well above, Part 2, Item 23, beginning "and now"), that this is the phase of Malchut of its Upper One, meaning the Malchut of Keter, which received the form of the will to receive, and by this renewal of form, the Malchut of Keter received a new name, which is Phase 1. And you already know, that when the spiritual acquires for itself a new form, it becomes distinct as an independent domain, so too the Malchut of Keter, which is the will to bestow that exists in the Emanator, when the will to emanate was born in it, as it were, surely it does not need actual vessels, God forbid, but rather its will immediately comes into actuality, meaning, that it received the form of the "will to receive," which is the first substance of the emanated being, as above, and this is called Phase 1.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:9
items.html:
The emergence of Malchut of Keter into Phase 1 is like lighting a candle from a candle, in which the first is not diminished.
And remember here, that there is no absence in the spiritual, and what is said, that Malchut of Keter received the form of Phase 1, does not mean that Malchut of Keter, God forbid, was absent and diminished from Keter, but rather that the Malchut of Keter remained in its first level without change, which is like lighting a candle from a candle, in which the first is not diminished, and that same Malchut of Keter that received Phase 1 was not diminished at all from Keter, but rather only a new phase was added, meaning, the Malchut of Keter remained in its place in all its perfection and level as before, except that another phase was added to the Malchut of Keter, meaning, the phase of Malchut that received Phase 1 and became the first substance in the Sefira of Hochma, and remember this for all that follows so as not to become confused.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:10
items.html:
After the first substance received the light, the vessel of Hochma itself was revealed.
Discernment 2 is the substance of that vessel after it has received its light, for then the vessel is completed and is called "Hochma," meaning, that before it received its light it is called only by the name of its own phase, namely Phase 1, and is not yet the phase of the vessel of Hochma, but rather Malchut of Keter. And this can be likened to a fetus in its mother's womb, which is not called by its name before it is born and receives the light and vitality that belong to it. So too the first substance, before it receives its light, is not yet called by the name Hochma, but is still included in Malchut of Keter, but afterward, when the substance draws its light, which is called Haya, then the vessel acquires its own particular name, namely "Hochma" (see well above, Item 27, beginning "and now"). And these two discernments should be understood in every single Sefira, namely: the vessel before it received the light, which is still discerned under the name of the Upper One, and the vessel after it received the light, for then it is considered in its own phase.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:11
items.html:
From the aspect of the first substance, Hochma is discerned as "not possible." And from the aspect that it is full of light, it is discerned as "not intending."
Now you will understand, that Phase 1, which is Hochma, is discerned as the phase of "not possible and not intending": for from the aspect of its first substance, which is Malchut of Keter, which received the renewal of the form of Phase 1, at the time when the Sefira of Hochma had not yet risen to a name before itself, as above, surely this revelation of the will to receive is discerned as "not possible," with respect to the Sefira of Hochma itself. And also from the aspect of Malchut of Keter, it is considered "not possible," for it is not possible for it to emanate Hochma without Hochma having the phase of "will to receive," for receiving the abundance without the will to receive it is compulsion and burden, the opposite of the intention of the Emanator, which is to do good and to give pleasure, as is known. And it is also discerned as "not intending," meaning that it has no drawing and yearning to receive the light. For you already know, that there is no completeness in the will before yearning and drawing toward the light has been revealed in it (as above, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 50, beginning "now," see there well). It was also explained there well, that the matter of yearning is revealed only at a time when the light and the abundance are not in the vessel, for then it is possible that it will yearn after it, but this cannot be revealed while the vessel is full of its light, see there well. And therefore, since the aforementioned vessel of Hochma is full of its own light, there is no longer any yearning in it for the abundance, and therefore Hochma is considered "not intending," meaning, that it has no drawing and yearning after the abundance, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:12
items.html:
The intensifying of the will in Bina is discerned as "possible." And from the aspect that this comes to it from the first substance, it is discerned as "not intending."
And Phase 2, which is Bina, is discerned as the phase of "possible and not intending": for from the aspect of its first substance (as above, Part 2, Item 29, beginning "and so," see there), which is the Malchut of its Upper One, namely the Malchut of Hochma, which received within it the renewal of the form of Phase 2, meaning, by means of the intensifying that it performed (as explained well above, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 50, beginning "and the reason," see there), this intensifying of the will is discerned as the phase of "possible," meaning, that it was possible for it not to arouse this intensifying of the will. And it is also discerned as the phase of "not intending," because it is the Malchut of Hochma, and it is full of its light, and therefore, the desire is not revealed in it, as above. And you should understand, that all the additional revelation of will that was made in Phase 2 beyond Phase 1 is only the phase of "possible," meaning, the intensifying of the will that it performed, which comes from the power of the emanated being itself (see there above, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 50, beginning "now").

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:13
items.html:
The light of Hochma was sufficient, and it was not compelled to intensify and draw Hassadim.
And it should not be asked, why is it that also Malchut of Keter, which became Phase 1 in the Sefira of Hochma, also had that same possibility not to receive the phase of renewal of the will to receive, and yet why is Phase 1 discerned as "not possible"? However, there is a great difference here, for Malchut of Keter had no possibility of emanating the emanated being without it having the "will to receive," as above, whereas Malchut of Hochma, which is the phase of the emanated being itself, could be entirely satisfied with its own phase of will to receive, without being aroused to the will to bestow, which is Phase 2, and drawing the light of Hassadim, because the light of Haya is entirely sufficient for the emanated being, and it needs no further addition whatsoever.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:14
items.html:
ZA is discerned as "not possible," because the light of Hochma was lacking to it.
And Phase 3, which is Zeir Anpin, is discerned as "not possible and intending." "Not possible" is, for the reason that after Phase 2 was aroused and drew the light of Hassadim, a phase of delay was thereby made over the light of Hochma in the emanated being, for the phase of the will to bestow is the opposite of Phase 1, which is the will to receive, where the light of Hochma is. And since the light of Hochma is the main vitality of the Partzuf, and is therefore called by the name Haya, as above, therefore the Malchut of Bina returned and drew the illumination of the light of Hochma into her light of Hassadim, and when the Malchut of Bina drew this and made this renewal of form, it emerged from Phase 2 and became Phase 3 (as above, Part 2, Item 30, beginning "and concerning," see there), which is called Zeir Anpin.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:15
items.html:
ZA is discerned as "intending," because it had a yearning for Hochma.
And in this drawing, which is Phase 3, we must discern two things: the first is "not possible," meaning, that it has no other counsel, because the light of Haya was lacking in the emanated being. And the second is "intending," for there is here a yearning after the illumination of Hochma that it drew, because it drew it at a time when it was empty of it, for Phase 2 was covering over the light of Hochma, as above, and has in it only the light of Hassadim without Hochma, therefore, its Malchut, which drew the illumination of Hochma, drew this in a manner of yearning, which is called "intending," as above. And therefore, the phase of Zeir Anpin is called "not possible and intending," as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:16
items.html:
Malchut is discerned as "possible," because it could have been satisfied with the Hochma in ZA. And as "intending," because it had a yearning.
And Phase 4, which is Malchut, is discerned as "possible and intending": "possible" is, for the reason that there already exists an illumination of Hochma in ZA, meaning, in Phase 3, as above, and the Malchut of ZA is not compelled to make this intensifying anew, in order to draw the light of Hochma in a greater measure than in Phase 3. And "intending" is, because this intensifying, after the light of Hochma, was made in a manner of yearning, meaning, at a time when it did not have the light of Hochma, at which time the desire is revealed, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:17
items.html:
The difference between the light of Hochma and the illumination of Hochma.
And it should not be asked here, since in Phase 3 there is an illumination of Hochma, as above, that this is why Phase 4 is called by the phase of "possible," so how is the yearning for the light of Hochma revealed in Phase 4? However, you should understand well, that there is a great difference between the illumination of Hochma and the light of Hochma. For the illumination of Hochma means, that the essence of the degree is the light of Hassadim, except that it receives an illumination from the light of Hochma, whereas the light of Hochma means, that the entire essence of the light is wholly Hochma, and does not include Hassadim at all. Now, for the vitality of the degree, the illumination of Hochma suffices as well, as exists in Phase 3, which is ZA, and therefore the Malchut of ZA, which intensified in its will to draw the light of Hochma, was not compelled to do this, but rather there was a phase of yearning in it after the essence of the light of Hochma, which is far higher than the phase of the illumination of Hochma that is in Phase 3. For with respect to the aforesaid light of Hochma, it is discerned as being empty of this light, and therefore it is possible that the desire for it be revealed after it, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 4:18
items.html:
Only Phase 4 is considered a vessel of receiving, because it is the phase of possible and intending.
And behold, it has been explained that not all wills are considered vessels of receiving, but only Phase 4, for the will is not considered a phase of receiving except under the two conditions "possible" and "intending," meaning: that it not be compelled to receive, and that "yearning to receive" be revealed in it. To exclude Phase 3, even though there is a yearning to receive there, meaning "intending," nevertheless, since it is compelled to receive, this being its compelled vitality as above, it is therefore not considered a vessel of receiving. And to exclude Phase 2, which, even though it is not compelled to receive, nevertheless, since there is no yearning there, it is not considered a vessel of receiving. And needless to say Phase 1, which has neither this nor that, for it is compelled to receive its light, which is its vitality, and also has no yearning in it, therefore it is certainly an entirely feeble will.
